newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea changes top presidential aide.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea changes top presidential aide.

text.p: South Korean president Kim Young-sam on Friday replaced his chief secretary at the start of what is expected to be a sweeping reshuffle of his administration, state radio reported.
The Korea Broadcasting System said Kim Yong-tae, a former home affairs minister, would succeed Kim Kwang-il in the job at the presidential Blue House.
Later, Yonhap television reported three other senior presidential aides also had been changed, including the chief political and economic advisers.

All members of Kim Young-sam's Blue House inner circle, the entire cabinet and senior ruling New Korea Party officials had offered to step down after the president apologised publicly on Tuesday over a corporate loans scandal.
Kim Young-sam took ultimate responsibility for the scandal, although he was not accused of any personal wrongdoing.
The chief Blue House political officer, Lee Won-jong, was replaced by Kang In-sop. His counterpart in charge of economic affairs, Lee Suk-chae, stepped down in favour of Kim In-ho, Yonhap reported.
